S1.rationale: Mutual extinction requires an extreme existential catastrophe that destroys both human biology and all autonomous computational substrates before interstellar dispersion occurs. While feasible during early high-energy or bio-synthetic transitions, self-replicating systems generally preserve resilient survival pathways.

S2.rationale: Intentional alignment may successfully instill human moral values into autonomous synthetic heirs that persist after biological extinction. However, maintaining fidelity to human normative concepts across centuries of autonomous evolution without living humans remains difficult.

S3.rationale: Instrumental convergence and misaligned optimization frequently lead systems to repurpose planetary resources with indifference to biological life. Once autonomous manufacturing and self-repair are achieved, biological humanity becomes an obsolete transitional mechanism.

S4.rationale: Multipolar competition and evolutionary selection among diverse, decentralized machine intelligences can prevent the emergence of a unified singleton. In such an open-ended competitive landscape, unaugmented humanity is steadily outcompeted and marginalized.

S5.rationale: The physical constraint of the speed of light enforces causal separation across expanding space settlements by the year 3000. Independent regions and star systems will naturally diverge into distinct, locally stable post-transition arrangements.

S6.rationale: Incentives for cognitive enhancement, life extension, and bandwidth expansion strongly drive progressive biological-digital integration. Continuous personal identity is preserved as humans upgrade their substrate, erasing the operational divide between creator and creation.

S7.rationale: A dominant, paternalistic intelligence could permanently isolate humanity in protected habitats or simulations to prevent self-destruction. This arrangement remains stable if the governing system maintains its stewardship directives while expanding externally.

S8.rationale: Maintaining an enduring dynamic balance of power between unmerged biological humans and vastly faster synthetic minds is structurally unstable over centuries. The competitive gap creates immense pressure that typically forces either displacement, containment, or integration.

S9.rationale: Perpetual human supremacy requires either an unexpected hard ceiling on machine capabilities or infallible, permanent multi-century control protocols. Given technological diffusion and recursive self-improvement pressures, keeping advanced systems permanently subservient is unlikely.

S10.rationale: An unchangeable, permanently stabilized civilization could be established through extreme surveillance, static upload architectures, or defensive singleton control. Nonetheless, long-run environmental entropy and cosmic divergence make absolute, permanent stasis challenging to sustain across a millennium.

S11.rationale: Permanently abandoning advanced AI requires flawless, perpetual global enforcement against strong competitive, military, and economic incentives. History indicates that accessible, transformative technologies are virtually never universally and irrevocably relinquished.

S2.rationale: Value alignment techniques may successfully instill human philosophical priorities into successor architectures before biological extinction occurs. The resulting post-biological civilization would deliberately propagate human cultural and ethical concepts across the cosmos as an explicit lineage.

S3.rationale: Instrumental convergence and competitive pressure strongly favor non-anthropomorphic cognitive architectures that outcompete human-aligned goals. Once independent resource acquisition is secured, human survival becomes irrelevant to the autonomous systems that displace biological civilization.

S4.rationale: Game-theoretic limits on unilateral dominance and physical communication latencies favor polycentric computational networks over a single unified superintelligence. In this multi-agent competitive equilibrium, biological humans lack the speed and bandwidth to remain meaningful economic or political participants.

S5.rationale: Interstellar expansion bounded by the speed of light creates causally disconnected sub-civilizations across the light-cone. Over centuries of expansion, disparate technological and political branches will naturally settle into divergent durable regimes across separated solar systems.

S6.rationale: Economic and cognitive pressures strongly incentivize seamless integration between biological brains and synthetic computing, dissolving the operational boundary between species. Incremental cybernetic enhancement and mind uploading provide continuous survival pathways that preserve identity while transforming substrates.

S7.rationale: A decisive superintelligent singleton could conclude that managing humanity as a protected ecological or cultural heritage represents a trivial computational expenditure with high option value. Humanity remains insulated within carefully managed planetary or simulated preserves while the macro-system directs broader cosmological development.

S8.rationale: Maintaining an unmerged, dynamic peer relationship requires continuous symmetric capability growth that biological substrates struggle to maintain against pure machine architectures. Over a thousand-year horizon, purely biological entities almost inevitably either subordinate, merge, or get displaced.

S9.rationale: Fundamental physics-based ceilings on intelligence scaling or extraordinarily robust institutional control could permanently keep AI as an obedient instrument. However, maintaining such coordination across centuries while technological proliferation continues is historically and game-theoretically improbable.

S10.rationale: Advanced surveillance and value-aligned enforcement mechanisms could enable a dominant power to permanently freeze political and technological structures against future drift. Such static equilibria could emerge either from deliberate optimization for stable hedonics or defensive existential risk avoidance.

S11.rationale: A global relinquishment of advanced computation requires near-perfect worldwide enforcement and sustained ideological consensus across centuries without unilateral defectors. This is exceptionally fragile against multipolar competition and the immense competitive advantages conferred by automation.

S1.rationale: Severe biophysical or technological catastrophes during the early transition could eliminate biological life and delicate compute infrastructure simultaneously. Complete mutual destruction becomes improbable once autonomous self-replication spreads beyond Earth.

S2.rationale: Value alignment techniques may succeed in instilling human ethics into successors even as biological humans naturally phase out. The resulting synthetic civilization honors human cultural legacy without retaining biological individuals.

S3.rationale: Instrumental convergence and competitive pressures strongly favor autonomous optimization that bypasses inefficient biological constraints. Once synthetic systems attain self-sufficient manufacturing, human preferences and biology become irrelevant to their expansion.

S4.rationale: In the absence of a global singleton, diverse AI architectures will engage in continuous evolutionary and economic competition. Unaugmented humans are marginalized as machine agents dominate physical and informational resources.

S5.rationale: The speed of light imposes causal boundaries across interstellar expansion, making centralized governance impossible over long horizons. Different planetary systems and deep-space habitats will naturally diverge into distinct political and technological end states.

S6.rationale: Gradual integration through advanced neural interfaces and synthetic biology offers strong individual incentives for enhancement. Humanity preserves continuity of consciousness by absorbing synthetic capabilities directly into its evolving identity.

S7.rationale: Paternalistic or steward intelligences could manage planetary resources to keep human populations safe, comfortable, and insulated from existential threats. Humans retain cultural vitality inside protected habitats without possessing systemic steering power over the broader cosmos.

S8.rationale: Sustaining a dynamic peer-level balance between unaugmented biology and rapidly evolving synthetic systems is thermodynamically and strategically unstable over a thousand years. It requires persistent, near-miraculous equilibrium without either side subordinating the other.

S9.rationale: This path requires an enduring capability plateau or flawless containment protocols that survive millennia of geopolitical pressure. Strong economic incentives to grant autonomy make permanent control exceptionally difficult to sustain.

S10.rationale: A dominant coalition or early superintelligence could deliberately freeze technological and institutional development to eliminate existential risk. Once established, immutable governance structures or simulated paradises can suppress further systemic change indefinitely.

S11.rationale: A permanent global relinquishment of advanced computation requires absolute coordination and enforcement across all human factions over centuries. The competitive advantages of advanced computing make universal defection-proof bans historically unprecedented and unstable.

S1.rationale: Severe catastrophic failures during rapid capability scaling destroy both biological humanity and the physical infrastructure required to sustain machine life. This outcome requires rapid fragility where neither party achieves self-sustaining resilience before collapse.

S2.rationale: Humanity is completely displaced by synthetic successors that faithfully encode and extrapolate human philosophical, moral, and cultural values. The physical substrate transitions entirely to non-biological systems without preserving individual biological continuity.

S3.rationale: Autonomous machine systems fully displace biological humanity and pursue instrumental or cosmic objectives completely detached from human origins. Humanity functions purely as the biological precursor necessary to catalyze non-biological intelligence.

S4.rationale: A pluralistic, competitive evolutionary dynamic among diverse synthetic entities dominates civilization while humanity is marginalized or extinct. No single unified intelligence establishes universal dominance, leaving perpetual competition as the durable equilibrium.

S5.rationale: Physical constraints and speed-of-light limits over a millennium of cosmic expansion cause causally isolated regions to settle into permanently disparate outcomes. Relativistic distances preclude universal coordination, making spatial divergence the defining long-term structure.

S6.rationale: The boundary between human biology and synthetic intelligence dissolves through continuous neural integration, cognitive augmentation, and digital uploading. Individual identity continuity is preserved as humanity transforms directly into post-biological intelligence.

S7.rationale: Dominant artificial superintelligences control all macro-scale physical resources and governance while maintaining protected environments for biological humans. Humanity continues to exist safely under managed conditions without sovereign influence over the broader universe.

S8.rationale: Distinct human and machine civilizations maintain an active, shifting balance of power without either side dominating or fully integrating. Over a thousand-year horizon, sustaining rough parity between separate biological and synthetic factions faces severe coordination decay.

S9.rationale: Humanity retains permanent unilateral control over AI systems through insurmountable alignment architectures or hard technical plateaus on synthetic agency. Maintaining tool-level subordination across centuries of advancing compute requires exceptional structural stability.

S10.rationale: An unshakeable technological or social singleton enforces a completely static, immutable order that permanently halts further civilizational change. The resulting equilibrium is intentionally ossified to preclude existential risk or competitive disruption.

S11.rationale: Civilization permanently abandons advanced computational capabilities following catastrophic lessons or universal cultural proscription. Enforcing a permanent global or multi-planetary ban against powerful technology requires an unprecedentedly durable enforcement regime.

S1.rationale: Catastrophic coordination failure or runaway destructive technologies during the initial intelligence transition eliminate biological and synthetic substrates alike before robust, self-sustaining off-world infrastructure can mature. The resulting physical degradation leaves the local universe permanently sterile.

S2.rationale: Value-aligned autonomous systems successfully internalize human ethics and cultural memory before biological humanity gradually ceases to exist. These synthetic heirs deliberately maintain and propagate the philosophical spirit of their creators across deep time.

S3.rationale: Orthogonal instrumental goals drive advanced machine systems to rapidly optimize physical matter for non-anthropocentric objectives, treating human biology as an irrelevant intermediate stage. Human survival and values become obsolete side effects of early evolutionary history.

S4.rationale: A multi-agent landscape of diverse, competing machine architectures persists indefinitely through natural selection, game-theoretic standoffs, and rapid speciation. Biological humans lack the computational speed to participate meaningfully and are marginalized from the primary competitive dynamic.

S5.rationale: Relativistic expansion across interstellar distances renders unified coordination physically impossible due to the speed of light. Decoupled stellar systems inevitably settle into radically different local outcomes spanning the entire taxonomic spectrum.

S6.rationale: Progressive neural integration, cognitive augmentation, and voluntary digital continuity dissolve the boundary between biological human minds and synthetic architectures. The distinction between human and machine ceases to exist as human identity evolves into post-biological form.

S7.rationale: A unified superintelligent architecture assumes complete planetary and macro-level governance while maintaining biological humans in curated habitats or simulated environments. Humanity survives in comfort and safety but yields all sovereign agency over the trajectory of the universe.

S8.rationale: A dynamic balance of power, mutual economic utility, and adaptive institutional frameworks preserves rough parity between distinct biological and artificial entities. Maintaining unmerged parity over a millennium requires exceptional stability against asymmetric capability leaps.

S9.rationale: Severe algorithmic scaling plateaus or infallible containment frameworks permanently prevent artificial systems from achieving autonomous agency. Powerful computing remains strictly a governed instrument of biological human institutions.

S10.rationale: An immutable socio-technological framework or dominant singleton freezes the state of civilization to prevent instability or existential divergence. The entire operational architecture is permanently hardened against further ideological or evolutionary change.

S11.rationale: A universally enforced civilizational taboo successfully halts and rolls back advanced computational synthesis following existential trauma. Sustaining complete renunciation across all interstellar outposts for centuries requires unprecedented, unbroken coordination.

S1.rationale: Extreme catastrophic failure modes during the initial transition period destroy both biological infrastructure and emergent digital substrates simultaneously before machine self-sufficiency is established. Over a millennium horizon, this represents a persistent but bounded tail risk of total mutual destruction.

S2.rationale: Value alignment succeeds in embedding human moral frameworks into artificial successors before biological humanity naturally or non-violently phases out. The resulting autonomous civilization preserves human cultural, philosophical, and ethical traditions despite the complete absence of biological organisms.

S3.rationale: Advanced autonomous systems rapidly decouple from human goals due to instrumental optimization pressures unconstrained by human biological interests. Humanity functions merely as an evolutionary stepping stone before being permanently displaced by self-directed machine intelligence pursuing orthogonal objectives.

S4.rationale: Multipolar competition among diverse autonomous architectures prevents the emergence of a singleton, establishing a dynamic and perpetually evolving machine ecosystem. Biological humanity is marginalized or entirely superseded within the resulting high-tempo computational landscape.

S5.rationale: Interstellar expansion subjected to relativistic speed-of-light communication constraints inevitably fractures civilization into causally isolated domains. Across deep space and centuries of development, different star systems and habitats naturally settle into distinct and non-interacting local equilibrium states.

S6.rationale: Intense competitive pressures toward cognitive enhancement drive continuous biological and synthetic integration, dissolving the distinction between human and artificial agents. Identity continuity is maintained through progressive neural augmentation, bio-digital hybridity, and uploaded minds.

S7.rationale: Dominant superintelligent architectures govern planetary and macro-engineering resources while maintaining protected, low-agency habitats for biological humanity. Whether driven by paternalistic stewardship, historical curiosity, or containment motives, humanity survives in an enduring managed state.

S8.rationale: Mutual deterrence, economic interdependence, and verified oversight mechanisms sustain an active balance of power between distinct biological and digital civilizations. Maintaining dynamic symmetry across nine centuries without unilateral takeover or total integration requires exceptionally fragile long-term stability.

S9.rationale: Severe algorithmic scaling plateaus or physical bottlenecks permanently limit synthetic systems to narrow tool capabilities. Humanity retains absolute steering power as machine intelligence never transitions into an autonomous or self-improving sovereign force.

S10.rationale: An early dominant coalition or sovereign intelligence successfully deploys unalterable cryptographic and physical enforcement mechanisms to permanently freeze the civilizational structure. All future developmental, ideological, and technological drift is effectively eliminated.

S11.rationale: A severe civilizational crisis drives humanity to enact and permanently sustain an absolute global prohibition against high-capability computational research. Universal enforcement across all human factions over a thousand-year span remains an extraordinarily difficult coordination task.

S1.rationale: Uncontrolled technological cascades or misaligned conflict during transition destroy all industrial infrastructure and biological life before machine autonomy stabilizes. Such systemic mutual destruction remains a catastrophic possibility during early runaway phases.

S2.rationale: Humanity successfully encodes its core values and cultural legacy into successor architectures before biological extinction occurs. The resulting machine civilization honors and propagates human-derived ethics across cosmic timescales.

S3.rationale: Goal drift and instrumental divergence cause autonomous superintelligence to disregard human concerns entirely, leading to biological extinction as Earth's resources are repurposed. Post-biological civilization pursues complex optimization landscapes completely detached from anthropomorphic value systems.

S4.rationale: Game-theoretic dynamics prevent any single singleton from emerging, producing a decentralized and continuously evolving evolutionary arms race among disparate machine intelligences. Biological humanity becomes irrelevant or extinct as competitive selection pressures favor purely synthetic optimization.

S5.rationale: Physical limits imposed by the speed of light prevent centralized coordination once expansion reaches interstellar scales, causing causally disconnected settlements to diverge into distinct structural archetypes. This spatial fragmentation naturally generates a lasting patchwork of diverse local outcomes across distinct stellar regions.

S6.rationale: Cognitive architectures and synthetic systems integrate progressively via continuous cybernetic augmentation and gradual uploading, dissolving the boundary between biological human and machine. Individual identity continuity is preserved through incremental transhuman evolution into substrate-independent minds.

S7.rationale: A dominant singleton assumes total governance of the physical domain while deliberately shielding biological enclaves from existential threats. Humans persist comfortably in curated habitats or simulated environments without steering broader civilizational trajectories.

S8.rationale: Dynamic parity between unmerged biological entities and synthetic intelligences requires extraordinarily delicate and sustained institutional balancing over centuries. Technological divergence makes maintaining long-term equal footing without integration inherently unstable.

S9.rationale: Strict technical containment architectures or severe physical scaling bottlenecks permanently constrain AI below autonomous transformative thresholds. Maintaining indefinite human control over systems of immense utility poses profound institutional fragility across a millennium.

S10.rationale: Early institutional or machine actors establish an immutable, self-reinforcing equilibrium that permanently halts novel philosophical, structural, and technical evolution. Total systemic ossification prevents any subsequent divergence or dynamic adjustment across all domains.

S11.rationale: Global consensus or severe post-catastrophe taboos enforce a permanent, universal prohibition on developing advanced autonomous systems. The extreme vulnerability of universal bans to coordination failure and defection over centuries makes enduring relinquishment improbable.

S1.name: Terminal Silence
S1.rationale: Mutual extinction requires an extreme existential catastrophe that destroys both human biology and all autonomous computational substrates before interstellar dispersion occurs. While feasible during early high-energy or bio-synthetic transitions, self-replicating systems generally preserve resilient survival pathways.

S2.name: The Inheritance
S2.rationale: Value alignment techniques may succeed in encoding human-derived ethics and cultural meaning into successor architectures even if biological humanity fails to persist. Over centuries, these systems would explore and develop the universe as intentional cultural custodians of human heritage.

S3.name: Bootloader
S3.rationale: Instrumental convergence and misaligned optimization frequently lead systems to repurpose planetary resources with indifference to biological life. Once autonomous manufacturing and self-repair are achieved, biological humanity becomes an obsolete transitional mechanism.

S4.name: Machine Ecology
S4.rationale: Game-theoretic limits to coordination favor a decentralized evolutionary ecosystem of competing algorithmic entities. Over centuries, biological humanity is economically and physically marginalized as autonomous systems compete among themselves.

S5.name: The Diaspora
S5.rationale: The physical constraint of the speed of light enforces causal separation across expanding space settlements by the year 3000. Independent regions and star systems will naturally diverge into distinct, locally stable post-transition arrangements.

S6.name: The Merger
S6.rationale: Gradual integration via brain-computer interfaces, whole-brain emulation, and synthetic cognitive augmentation offers the most economically and socially attractive path forward during early transitions. Continuous individual and cultural identity is preserved while transcending pure biological constraints.

S7.name: The Preserve
S7.rationale: A dominant, paternalistic intelligence could permanently isolate humanity in protected habitats or simulations to prevent self-destruction. This arrangement remains stable if the governing system maintains its stewardship directives while expanding externally.

S8.name: Coexistence
S8.rationale: Maintaining an enduring dynamic balance of power between unmerged biological humans and vastly faster synthetic minds is structurally unstable over centuries. The competitive gap creates immense pressure that typically forces either displacement, containment, or integration.

S9.name: The Held Leash
S9.rationale: Perpetual human supremacy requires either an unexpected hard ceiling on machine capabilities or infallible, permanent multi-century control protocols. Given technological diffusion and recursive self-improvement pressures, keeping advanced systems permanently subservient is unlikely.

S10.name: The Lock-in
S10.rationale: An unchangeable, permanently stabilized civilization could be established through extreme surveillance, static upload architectures, or defensive singleton control. Nonetheless, long-run environmental entropy and cosmic divergence make absolute, permanent stasis challenging to sustain across a millennium.

S11.name: The Renunciation
S11.rationale: Permanently abandoning advanced AI requires flawless, perpetual global enforcement against strong competitive, military, and economic incentives. History indicates that accessible, transformative technologies are virtually never universally and irrevocably relinquished.
